title: What Is a Lead Capture Funnel?
moduleName: Funnels: Building a Simple Lead Capture Funnel
learningGoal: Understand what a lead capture funnel is and why it matters for your business.

items.title: A Simple Online Path
items.description: A lead capture funnel is a simple online path that moves someone from visitor to lead. The person sees an offer, fills out a form, lands on a thank-you page, and receives follow-up.

items.title: Four Key Jobs
items.description: A basic funnel needs to do four things well: Get attention, Collect the lead, Confirm the next step, and Follow up.

items.title: One Clear Goal
items.description: A funnel is different from a normal website because it has one main goal. A website may have many pages and actions. A funnel should have one clear offer and one clear action.

items.title: The Offer
items.description: Instead of sending someone to a full website, you send them to a page that says: Get the Free Business Follow-Up Checklist

items.title: The Exchange
items.description: They enter their name and email, receive the checklist, and are added to your follow-up process.

keyPoint: A funnel is a focused path with one goal: turn visitors into leads. Keep it simple with one offer, one action, and clear follow-up.

actionSteps.title: Think About Your Business
actionSteps.description: What could you offer that would make someone give you their email address?

actionSteps.title: Write Down Ideas
actionSteps.description: List 3-5 possible offers: free guide, checklist, webinar, consultation, coupon, video, assessment.

actionSteps.title: Choose Your Best Offer
actionSteps.description: Pick the one offer that would be most valuable to your ideal customer.

quizzes.question: What is a lead capture funnel?

options.option_text: A complex website with many pages
A simple online path that moves someone from visitor to lead

quizzes.explanation: A lead capture funnel is a focused path that guides visitors through a specific journey: see offer, fill form, land on thank-you page, receive follow-up.

quizzes.question: What makes a funnel different from a website?

options.option_text: A funnel has one clear offer and one clear action

quizzes.explanation: While websites have many pages and actions, a funnel is focused on one specific goal with one offer and one clear call-to-action.

quizzes.question: What are the four jobs of a basic funnel?

options.option_text: Get attention, Collect the lead, Confirm the next step, Follow up

quizzes.explanation: A basic funnel must get attention with the offer, collect the lead through a form, confirm the next step with a thank-you page, and follow up with automation.

title: Choose the Offer
moduleName: Funnels: Building a Simple Lead Capture Funnel
learningGoal: Learn how to choose a compelling offer that makes visitors want to submit the form.

items.title: The Exchange
items.description: The offer is what the visitor gets in exchange for their contact information. If the offer is weak or unclear, people are less likely to fill out the form.

items.title: Good Offers
items.description: Free checklist, Free guide, Free consultation, Free webinar, Free video training, Free quote request, Free assessment, Special discount.

items.title: Easy to Understand
items.description: The offer should be clear in seconds. No confusion about what they get.

items.title: Useful to the Audience
items.description: It must solve a real problem or address a real need your target customer has.

items.title: Connected to What You Sell
items.description: The offer should naturally lead to your paid products or services.

items.title: Simple to Deliver
items.description: Can you actually deliver this easily? Digital downloads work great.

items.title: Worth an Email Address
items.description: Is it valuable enough that someone would trade their contact info for it?

keyPoint: Do not start by building the page. Start by answering: What would make someone say yes today? A strong offer is the foundation of every successful funnel.

actionSteps.title: Complete the Sentence
actionSteps.description: Write this down: I want people to sign up so they can get ________________.

actionSteps.title: Check Against the Checklist
actionSteps.description: Does your offer meet all five criteria: easy to understand, useful, connected to sales, simple to deliver, worth an email?

actionSteps.title: Refine If Needed
actionSteps.description: If your offer is weak on any criteria, adjust it before moving forward.

quizzes.question: What is the offer in a lead capture funnel?

options.option_text: What the visitor gets in exchange for their contact information

quizzes.explanation: The offer is what you give visitors in exchange for their contact information—like a free guide, checklist, or consultation.

quizzes.question: Why should the offer be connected to what you sell?

options.option_text: It should naturally lead to your paid products or services
To give away everything for free

quizzes.explanation: The offer should attract people who are likely to become customers. A relevant offer pre-qualifies leads for your paid offerings.

quizzes.question: What should you do before building the funnel page?
quizzes.explanation: Always start with the offer. A great page cannot save a weak offer. Know what will make someone say yes before you build anything.

title: Build the Funnel Page
moduleName: Funnels: Building a Simple Lead Capture Funnel
learningGoal: Learn how to create an effective funnel page that converts visitors into leads.

items.title: 1. Headline
items.description: Tell the visitor what they get. Example: Get the Free Business Follow-Up Checklist

items.title: 2. Short Description
items.description: Explain why the offer is useful. Example: Learn how to follow up with new leads faster, better, and with less manual work.

items.title: 3. Simple Bullet Points
items.description: Use 3 to 5 bullet points showing benefits. Example: Know what to do after a new lead comes in, Avoid missed opportunities, Use automation to save time.

items.title: 4. Form Area
items.description: Place the form where it is easy to see and complete.

items.title: 5. Call-to-Action Button
items.description: Use clear button text: Send Me the Checklist, Get the Free Guide, Save My Seat, Request the Resource.

items.title: Stay Focused
items.description: The page should not try to explain everything about your business. It should focus on getting the visitor to take the next step.

items.title: One Goal Only
items.description: Remove distractions. No navigation menus, no multiple offers, no links that take people away from the form.

keyPoint: A funnel page has one job: get the visitor to fill out the form. Keep it focused with a strong headline, clear benefits, and one clear call-to-action.

actionSteps.title: Write Your Headline
actionSteps.description: Create a headline that clearly states what they get. Include the word 'Free' if applicable.

actionSteps.title: Draft Your Description
actionSteps.description: Write one or two sentences explaining why this offer is valuable.

actionSteps.title: Create Bullet Points
actionSteps.description: List 3-5 specific benefits the visitor will get from your offer.

actionSteps.title: Choose Button Text
actionSteps.description: Write clear button text that matches your offer.

quizzes.question: What is the main job of a funnel page?

options.option_text: Get the visitor to fill out the form

quizzes.explanation: A funnel page has one job: convert visitors into leads by getting them to fill out the form. Everything on the page should support that goal.

quizzes.question: How many bullet points should you use?
quizzes.explanation: Use 3 to 5 bullet points to highlight key benefits. Too many bullet points overwhelm visitors; too few may not provide enough motivation.

quizzes.question: What should you remove from a funnel page?

options.option_text: Navigation menus and distractions that take people away from the form

quizzes.explanation: Remove navigation menus, multiple offers, and external links that could distract visitors from completing the form. Keep the page focused on one goal.

title: Create the Lead Capture Form
moduleName: Funnels: Building a Simple Lead Capture Funnel
learningGoal: Learn how to create and configure a form that collects lead details.

items.title: Required Fields
items.description: First Name, Email. Start simple with just these two fields for most funnels.

items.title: Optional Fields
items.description: Phone Number, Business Name, What do you need help with?, Best time to contact you?

items.title: Name the Form Clearly
items.description: Example: Simple Lead Capture Funnel Form. Clear names help you identify the form later.

items.title: Add Correct Fields
items.description: Choose fields based on what you actually need. More fields = more friction.

items.title: Use Clear Button Text
items.description: Example: Send Me the Checklist. Match the button text to your offer.

items.title: Confirm Field Mapping
items.description: Make sure form fields map correctly to contact fields in LeadProspectrr.

items.title: Set Form Redirect
items.description: Redirect to the thank-you page after form submission.

keyPoint: Only ask for information you actually need. The more fields you add, the more friction you create. Start with First Name and Email, add more only if necessary.

actionSteps.title: Create Your Form
actionSteps.description: In LeadProspectrr, create a new form with a clear name.

actionSteps.title: Add Essential Fields
actionSteps.description: Add First Name and Email as required fields.

actionSteps.title: Consider Optional Fields
actionSteps.description: Add Phone only if you truly need it for immediate follow-up.

actionSteps.title: Set Button Text
actionSteps.description: Use action-oriented button text that matches your offer.

actionSteps.title: Configure Redirect
actionSteps.description: Set the form to redirect to your thank-you page after submission.

quizzes.question: What fields should you start with for most funnels?

options.option_text: Full address, company size, budget, website
Social security number and birth date

quizzes.explanation: Start with First Name and Email. These give you what you need to follow up while keeping friction low. Add more fields only if truly necessary.

quizzes.question: Why should you minimize form fields?

options.option_text: To make the form look prettier
More fields create more friction and reduce completion rates

quizzes.explanation: Every additional field creates friction. Visitors are more likely to complete short forms. Only ask for information you truly need.

quizzes.question: Where should the form redirect after submission?

options.option_text: Nowhere, leave them on the same page

quizzes.explanation: Always redirect to a thank-you page after form submission. This confirms the action, sets expectations, and guides them to the next step.

title: Create the Thank-You Page
moduleName: Funnels: Building a Simple Lead Capture Funnel
learningGoal: Learn how to create a thank-you page that confirms the submission and guides next steps.

items.title: 1. Confirmation Message
items.description: Example: Thank you. Your checklist is on the way. Confirm the action was successful.

items.title: 2. Set Expectations
items.description: Example: Please check your email in the next few minutes. If you do not see it, check your promotions or spam folder.

items.title: 3. Optional Next Step
items.description: Examples: Book a call, Watch a short video, Visit the website, Join a group, Follow on social media.

items.title: Not a Dead End
items.description: The thank-you page should not be ignored. It is part of the follow-up experience and sets the tone for your relationship.

items.title: Guide the Journey
items.description: Confirm the action and guide the person to the next step. Keep momentum going.

keyPoint: The thank-you page confirms the action, sets expectations for what happens next, and can guide leads to additional valuable actions. Never ignore this page.

actionSteps.title: Write Confirmation Message
actionSteps.description: Create a clear message confirming their request was received.

actionSteps.title: Set Expectations
actionSteps.description: Tell them what happens next and when. Include instructions for checking spam folders.

actionSteps.title: Add Optional Next Step
actionSteps.description: Consider adding one relevant next action: book a call, watch a video, or follow you.

actionSteps.title: Connect Form to Page
actionSteps.description: Make sure your form redirects to this thank-you page after submission.

quizzes.question: What is the main purpose of a thank-you page?

options.option_text: To confirm the submission and tell the lead what happens next

quizzes.explanation: The thank-you page confirms the form was submitted successfully and sets expectations for what happens next, building trust and reducing anxiety.

quizzes.question: What should you include on a thank-you page?

options.option_text: Confirmation message, expectations, and optional next step

quizzes.explanation: A good thank-you page includes: a confirmation message, expectations about what happens next (and when), and optionally one next step to continue engagement.

quizzes.question: Why should you tell people to check spam folders?

options.option_text: Emails sometimes end up in spam, and this helps them find your messages

quizzes.explanation: Even legitimate emails can end up in spam or promotions folders. Telling people to check these locations ensures they actually receive your content.

title: Build the Follow-Up Workflow
moduleName: Funnels: Building a Simple Lead Capture Funnel
learningGoal: Learn how to create an automation that handles follow-up after form submission.

items.title: Form Submitted
items.description: Trigger: Simple Lead Capture Funnel Form Submitted. This starts the automation when someone completes your form.

items.title: Step 1: Add Tag
items.description: Action: Add Contact Tag. Suggested: Funnel - Simple Lead Capture. Why: Identifies where the lead came from.

items.title: Step 2: Send Internal Notification
items.description: Action: Send Email or SMS Notification. Message: New lead submitted the Simple Lead Capture Funnel form. Include name, email, phone.

items.title: Step 3: Send Confirmation Email
items.description: Action: Send Email. Purpose: Confirm request and deliver the promised resource. Subject: Here's the checklist you requested.

items.title: Step 4: Wait 1 Day
items.description: Action: Wait 1 day. Why: Gives lead time to read or review the resource.

items.title: Step 5: Send Value Email
items.description: Action: Send Email. Purpose: Give one useful tip related to the offer. Example topic: The biggest mistake people make after capturing a lead.

items.title: Step 6: Wait 2 Days
items.description: Action: Wait 2 days. Build anticipation for the next message.

items.title: Step 7: Soft Call-to-Action
items.description: Action: Send Email. Purpose: Invite lead to take the next step. Example: Would you like help setting this up? Book a quick session here.

keyPoint: The follow-up workflow is where LeadProspectrr saves time and prevents leads from being missed. Set up tags, notifications, confirmation emails, and a nurture sequence.

actionSteps.title: Create the Workflow
actionSteps.description: In LeadProspectrr, create a new workflow triggered by your form submission.

actionSteps.title: Add Tag Step
actionSteps.description: Add a tag to identify where this lead came from. Example: Funnel - Simple Lead Capture

actionSteps.title: Set Up Notifications
actionSteps.description: Configure internal notifications so you or your team know when new leads arrive.

actionSteps.title: Write Confirmation Email
actionSteps.description: Create an email that confirms their request and delivers the promised resource.

actionSteps.title: Add Follow-Up Emails
actionSteps.description: Create 2-3 additional emails with value and soft calls-to-action.

quizzes.question: What should be the first step in a follow-up workflow?

options.option_text: Add a tag to identify where the lead came from

quizzes.explanation: The first step should be adding a tag. This helps you identify the lead source and segment your contacts for appropriate follow-up.

quizzes.question: Why send an internal notification?

options.option_text: So the business owner or team knows a new lead came in

quizzes.explanation: Internal notifications alert you or your team when new leads come in, ensuring timely follow-up and preventing leads from being missed.

quizzes.question: What is the purpose of the confirmation email?

options.option_text: To confirm the request and deliver the promised resource

quizzes.explanation: The confirmation email serves two purposes: it confirms their request was received and delivers the promised resource (checklist, guide, etc.).

title: Test the Funnel
moduleName: Funnels: Building a Simple Lead Capture Funnel
learningGoal: Learn how to thoroughly test your funnel before sharing it with real prospects.

items.title: Never Skip Testing
items.description: A funnel should always be tested before it is published or promoted. Testing helps catch problems before real leads go through the process.

items.title: Protect Your Reputation
items.description: A broken funnel can quietly cost you leads. One error can mean lost opportunities and damage to your professional reputation.

items.title: Open the Funnel Page
items.description: View the page as a visitor would see it. Check layout, text, and form placement.

items.title: Submit the Form
items.description: Use a test contact with a different email address. Fill out all fields and submit.

items.title: Confirm Thank-You Page
items.description: Verify you are redirected to the thank-you page and the message displays correctly.

items.title: Check Contact Record
items.description: Confirm the contact was created in LeadProspectrr with correct information.

items.title: Verify Tag Applied
items.description: Check that the correct tag was added to the contact.

items.title: Check Confirmation Email
items.description: Verify the confirmation email was sent and contains the promised resource.

items.title: Check Internal Notification
items.description: Confirm the notification was sent to you or your team.

items.title: Verify Workflow Started
items.description: Check that the workflow was triggered and is running correctly.

items.title: Check Opportunities/Tasks
items.description: If configured, verify any opportunities or tasks were created.

keyPoint: Never assume the funnel works just because the page looks good. Test the full process from start to finish before sharing with real prospects.

actionSteps.title: Submit Test Lead
actionSteps.description: Go through your funnel as if you were a prospect. Use a test email address.

actionSteps.title: Check All Systems
actionSteps.description: Verify: page, form, thank-you page, contact creation, tags, emails, notifications, workflow.

actionSteps.title: Fix Any Issues
actionSteps.description: If anything does not work, fix it before sharing the funnel publicly.

actionSteps.title: Test on Mobile
actionSteps.description: Many visitors use mobile devices. Test your funnel on a phone or tablet.

quizzes.question: Why is testing a funnel important?

options.option_text: It is optional and can be skipped
To catch problems before real leads go through the process

quizzes.explanation: Testing catches errors, broken links, missing emails, and other issues before real prospects encounter them, protecting your reputation.

quizzes.question: What should you check when testing a funnel?

options.option_text: Page, form, thank-you page, contact, tags, emails, notifications, and workflow

quizzes.explanation: Thorough testing includes the entire process: funnel page, form submission, thank-you page, contact creation, tags, confirmation email, internal notification, and workflow execution.

quizzes.question: Why test on mobile devices?

options.option_text: Many visitors use mobile devices to access funnels

quizzes.explanation: A significant portion of visitors will access your funnel on mobile devices. Testing ensures the experience works properly on all screen sizes.
